decisions.what: W_STYLE_UNKNOWN fires only when the block has at least one server-registered style; markup-mode wp_verify does not see per-block custom css unless the harvested page contains that block.
decisions.why: Many core styles (image rounded, button outline) register client-side only — warning on every such use would be noise; and WordPress itself emits per-block custom css conditionally on block presence, so url-mode verify against a page containing the block is the honest oracle for rung-5 css.

decisions.what: wp_validate's binding/style checks run server-side through POST /validate; the agent-local pre-check remains TreeIR-schema-only.
decisions.why: The checks need the styles registry and binding sources at the current fingerprint — exactly what the server has and the local pre-check exists to avoid fetching.

decisions.what: Kept variations_count beside the new blocks[].variations despite the spec's 'replaces' wording.
decisions.why: The spec's own version_policy (v1 clients keep working) outranks the section prose; removing a v1 field is a wire break.

decisions.what: bindable_attributes ships as a version-aware vendored map (paragraph/heading/image/button) behind the x_companion_bindable_attributes filter.
decisions.why: Core hardcodes the allowlist in a local variable inside WP_Block::process_block_bindings — not reflectable; the map mirrors canon verbatim and the filter adopts future core expansion without a release.

decisions.what: Block style source labels are best-effort: 'theme' when the style name appears in theme-origin theme.json variations for that block, 'agent' when tracked by the schema provides option, else 'plugin'.
decisions.why: register_block_style() does not record its caller; no API exposes registration provenance.

decisions.what: No new cache-invalidation hooks for model changes: the platform stamp is a fingerprint input and the manifest transient is keyed by fingerprint.
decisions.why: Registration happens on init before any REST read; the fingerprint IS the invalidator by construction, and hooks like registered_post_type fire on every request.

deviations.spec_ref: M5 acceptance: 'uninstall leaves no registrations (asserted via data_model diff)'
deviations.what: Live uninstall is asserted by the gate's sandbox probes (deactivate -> fresh-request data-model diff, per package, every build), not by a live delete route — the spec's rest_api_additions define install + installed only.
deviations.why: A DELETE /schema/{slug} route is real surface area the spec deliberately did not include; adding it silently would be scope growth. The uninstall guarantee is still proven on every gate run.
